ai.description: The Assam Treefrog (Hylidae) reaches 3–5 cm. It is typically olive-green or brown with a dark lateral stripe and orange-spotted flanks. Distinctive features include large toe discs and webbed feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hyla annectans* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark lateral stripe extending from the snout through the eye to the flank, which is absent in most other Indian treefrogs.
ai.habitat: The Assam treefrog inhabits subtropical broadleaf forests and montane vegetation at altitudes ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Assam treefrog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the vegetation near forest streams and ponds.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hyla annectans* is oviparous, breeding during the monsoon (May–August). Females lay small clutches of eggs in or near stagnant water bodies, which hatch into aquatic larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hyla annectans* occurs in Northeast India (Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Mizoram) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting elevations between 500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Assam Treefrog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "peep-peep" notes, typically heard emanating from vegetation near ponds or marshes during the monsoon.
